accepted.s: Between 2001 and 2011, India's urban population increased from approximately
accepted.x: India's urban population increased from 286 million in 2001 to 377.1 million in 2011, an increase of about 31.8%.
accepted.tq: Use the exact population pair rather than confusing absolute increase with percentage growth.
accepted.sec: Urban growth 2001-2011 - components behind absolute urban increase, causes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: For the first time since Independence, the absolute increase in India's urban population during 2001–2011
o: was equal to the rural increase
was smaller than the rural increase
accepted.x: Urban areas added about 91.0 million people, compared with a rural increase of about 90.4 million, making it the first such decade since Independence.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of comparison using the absolute figures rather than the percentages.
accepted.sec: Urban growth 2001-2011 - components behind absolute urban increase, causes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the principal reason for the sharp increase in India's urban population during 2001–2011?
o: Reclassification of erstwhile rural areas as urban
Reduction in the number of census towns
accepted.x: The principal reason was the reclassification of rural areas as urban. Census towns increased from 1,362 to 3,894 during this period.
accepted.tq: Identify the main cause instead of choosing a related but unsupported demographic factor.
accepted.sec: Urban growth 2001-2011 - components behind absolute urban increase, causes  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the components of urban growth:
1. Natural increase in population
2. Net rural-urban migration
3. Reclassification of rural areas as urban
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Natural increase, rural-urban migration and reclassification or creation of new towns are the three identified components of urban growth.
accepted.tq: Check whether all three recognised components are included before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Urban growth 2001-2011 - components behind absolute urban increase, causes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a cause of urbanisation in India?
o: Pressure of population on rural land
accepted.x: Growth of industry and trade, pressure on rural land, low farm productivity, services and transport are identified causes. The complete disappearance of transport services is not a cause stated in this context.
accepted.tq: Find the extreme reversal of a recognised development factor.
accepted.sec: Urban growth 2001-2011 - components behind absolute urban increase, causes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Delhi Development Authority was established under the
accepted.x: The Delhi Development Authority was set up under the Delhi Development Act, 1957.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the enabling legislation from nearby municipal and territorial laws.
accepted.sec: Urban planning institutions - FIRST urban development authority, planned cities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following planned cities is associated with Le Corbusier?
accepted.x: Chandigarh is the planned city associated with the architect Le Corbusier.
accepted.tq: Match the named planner with the correct planned city.
accepted.sec: Urban planning institutions - FIRST urban development authority, planned cities  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are recognised planned cities or planned urban settlements?
1. Chandigarh
2. Bhubaneswar
3. Gandhinagar
4. Navi Mumbai
5. Jamshedpur
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Chandigarh, Bhubaneswar, Gandhinagar, Navi Mumbai and Jamshedpur are all listed as planned cities or planned urban settlements. Jamshedpur is specifically noted as a planned industrial town.
accepted.tq: Test a complete named list and avoid excluding the industrial planned town.
accepted.sec: Urban planning institutions - FIRST urban development authority, planned cities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which institution is responsible for the greenfield capital Amaravati in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation בלבד
Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority
accepted.x: Amaravati is run by the Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority, commonly abbreviated as APCRDA.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority-location match to distinguish a state capital-region body from urban local bodies.
accepted.sec: Urban planning institutions - FIRST urban development authority, planned cities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many posts were created for the land pooling phases of Amaravati?
accepted.x: Ninety-five posts were created for the land pooling phases of Amaravati.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact administrative figure among close numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Urban planning institutions - FIRST urban development authority, planned cities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the Economic Survey 2025–26, every million-plus city should have a statutory City Spatial and Economic Plan covering
accepted.x: Every million-plus city is expected to have a statutory 20-year City Spatial and Economic Plan.
accepted.tq: Test the planning horizon directly, where nearby durations act as numerical traps.
accepted.sec: Urban planning institutions - FIRST urban development authority, planned cities  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The urban shares were 10.84% in 1901, 11.99% in 1931, 17.97% in 1961 and 27.81% in 2001.
accepted.tq: Match each census year with its percentage and eliminate shifted values.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Census years in ascending order of the urban share of population:
A. 1901
B. 1931
C. 1961
D. 2011
accepted.x: The urban shares were 10.84% in 1901, 11.99% in 1931, 17.97% in 1961 and 31.16% in 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the numerical trend from the earliest to the latest census year.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The period 1901–1931 is described as which phase of urban growth in India?
accepted.x: The period 1901–1931 was the slow phase, with urban growth of about 0.35% a year.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among the three named phases by matching the period with its label.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During the slow phase of urban growth between 1901 and 1931, the number of towns in India in 1931 was approximately
accepted.x: There were 2,049 towns in 1931. The figure of about 1,827 refers to 1901 and 7,935 to 2011.
accepted.tq: Place the town count in its correct census year rather than using the phase alone.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which period represented the medium phase of urban growth in India?
accepted.x: The medium phase extended from 1931 to 1961, during which the number of towns rose from 2,049 to 2,330.
accepted.tq: Match the phase label with the correct time interval and town-count trend.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the rapid phase of India's urban growth?
o: 1901 onwards, with urban population rising from 33.46 million to 78.94 million
2001 onwards, with urban population rising from 78.94 million to 286 million
1931 onwards, with urban population rising from 33.46 million to 286 million
1961 onwards, with urban population rising from 78.94 million to 377.11 million
accepted.x: The rapid phase began in 1961 and continued thereafter; urban population rose from 78.94 million in 1961 to 377.11 million in 2011, an increase of about 262%.
accepted.tq: Match both endpoints and the starting year instead of relying on only one figure.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the figures 31.80% and 31.16% associated with urbanisation in India?
o: 31.80% is the rural share and 31.16% is the decadal urban growth
31.80% is the decadal urban growth and 31.16% is the 2011 urban share
31.80% is the 2011 urban share and 31.16% is the rural share
Both figures represent the 2011 urban share
accepted.x: The 2011 Census urban share was 31.16%, while 31.80% is used in one heading to denote decadal urban growth.
accepted.tq: Separate two look-alike percentages by asking what each percentage measures.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 2011, the rural and urban shares of India's population were, respectively,
accepted.x: In 2011, the rural population accounted for 68.84% and the urban population for 31.16%.
accepted.tq: Test complementary shares and avoid reversing the rural-urban order.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The urban and rural populations added during 2001–2011 were approximately
accepted.x: Urban areas added about 91.0 million people and rural areas added about 90.4 million during 2001–2011.
accepted.tq: Read the comparison in the stated order and distinguish absolute increase from population share.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are indicators of urbanisation?
1. Number of towns
2. Urban share of population
3. Average size of an urban centre
4. Urban density
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The number of towns, urban share, urban growth rate, average size of urban centres and urban density are all indicators of urbanisation.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete indicator set rather than treating urbanisation as only a population-share measure.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's urban population is projected to reach approximately what level by 2031?
accepted.x: India's urban population is projected to reach about 60 crore by 2031.
accepted.tq: Use the projected absolute population figure, not the separate percentage projection.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Urbanisation level by 2031 — 31% according to the Sixteenth Finance Commission
Urbanisation level by 2031 — 41% according to the Sixteenth Finance Commission
Urbanisation level by 2031 — 51% according to the Sixteenth Finance Commission
Urbanisation level by 2031 — 61% according to the Sixteenth Finance Commission
accepted.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission projection places India's urbanisation level at 41% by 2031.
accepted.tq: Match the projection with the correct percentage and authority.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the stated projection, more than half of India's population is expected to be urban by
accepted.x: More than 50% of India's population is projected to be urban by 2050.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of crossing 50% from the earlier 2031 projections.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to World Urbanization Prospects 2025, cities account for approximately what share of the world's population?
accepted.x: World Urbanization Prospects 2025 reports that cities hold about 45% of the world's population.
accepted.tq: Test the global urban share independently of India's national figures.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct order of the four most populous cities mentioned in the global urbanisation projection?
accepted.x: The order given is Jakarta, Dhaka, Tokyo and New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Preserve the stated ranking order and avoid substituting familiar global city rankings.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The World Cities Report 2026 stated that approximately how many people face housing shortages?
accepted.x: About 40% of the world's population, approximately 3.4 billion people, face housing shortages according to the report.
accepted.tq: Link the percentage and absolute estimate rather than confusing it with the slum population.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which organisation is associated with the World Cities Report 2026?
accepted.x: The World Cities Report 2026 was issued by UN-Habitat and released at the World Urban Forum in Baku.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation-report association and reject neighbouring international bodies.
accepted.sec: Urbanisation trends since 1901 - decadal growth of urban population  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A town with a population of 1,00,000 or more belongs to which class under the class-size classification of towns?
accepted.x: Class I towns have a population of 1,00,000 and above.
accepted.tq: Apply the threshold directly, paying attention to the inclusive lower limit.
accepted.sec: Class-size classification of towns (Class I to VI) - population thresholds

accepted.s: Which one of the following population ranges corresponds to Class II towns?
accepted.x: Class II towns have populations ranging from 50,000 to 99,999.
accepted.tq: Match the class label with its exact range and distinguish adjacent classes.
accepted.sec: Class-size classification of towns (Class I to VI) - population thresholds

accepted.s: Which population range belongs to Class IV towns?
accepted.x: Class IV towns have populations between 10,000 and 19,999.
accepted.tq: Distinguish consecutive five-digit threshold bands.
accepted.sec: Class-size classification of towns (Class I to VI) - population thresholds

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I (Class)
a. Class I
b. Class II
c. Class V
d. Class VI
List-II (Population)
i. Less than 5,000
ii. 50,000–99,999
iii. 1,00,000 and above
iv. 5,000–9,999
accepted.x: Class I is 1,00,000 and above, Class II is 50,000–99,999, Class V is 5,000–9,999 and Class VI is below 5,000.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure extreme pairs and then verify the remaining class thresholds.
accepted.sec: Class-size classification of towns (Class I to VI) - population thresholds

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the size structure of India's towns is correct?
1. Class I cities contain about 70% of the urban population.
2. India has roughly 9,000 towns.
3. Only about 500 towns are large cities.
4. Most towns have populations below one lakh.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: Class I cities hold about 70% of the urban population, India has roughly 9,000 towns, only about 500 are large cities, and most towns have fewer than one lakh people.
accepted.tq: Check the complete size-structure description before choosing the all-inclusive option.
accepted.sec: Class-size classification of towns (Class I to VI) - population thresholds

accepted.s: The concentration of approximately 70 per cent of India's urban population in Class I cities indicates that urban growth is
accepted.x: The dominance of Class I cities in urban population indicates a top-heavy pattern of urban growth.
accepted.tq: Infer the structural pattern from the distribution of population among town classes.
accepted.sec: Class-size classification of towns (Class I to VI) - population thresholds
